newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Gadoon Textile up 11.89 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Gadoon Textile up 11.89 pct.

text.p: Pakistan's Gadoon Textile Mills Ltd rose 4.25 rupees, or 11.89 percent, to 40 on Tuesday on expectations that the caretaker government will soon announce a relief package for the textile sector, dealers said.
A turnover of 18,500 shares of the company was recorded at the Karachi bourse by midsession.
Gadoon shares fell back later and were last traded at 38.50 rupees each, up 2.75 on Monday's close.
"Mainly speculators are active in the textile sector on hopes of a government relief package. But the rise appears temporary," dealer Sameer Ahmed of ING Baring Securities said.

"The government's textile reform package could be good for the economy as over 60 percent of Pakistan's exports are cotton-based. But we do not expect a turnaround in textile companies," dealer Ather Raouf of Carr Mashriq said.
"One reform package cannot pull textile companies out of trouble, most of which have years of accumulated losses."

He said Gadoon Textile was considered one of the better companies due to the exemptions it enjoys because of its location. "But the company's very strength is its weakness because the government is under pressure from the IMF to withdraw concessions given to various sectors."

Dealer Sameer Ahmed said that the textile industry had over-expanded in earlier years. "Only a few good, professionally managed companies that have survived the slump in this sector could gain as a result of any relief package," Ahmed said.
